title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
oneLiner: The definitive architecture manual for reliability, scalability, storage engines, and consensus algorithms.
keyLearnings: LSM-Trees vs B-Trees: LSM trades read-amplification for high sequential write throughput; B-Trees optimize point reads with in-place page updates.
Linearizability vs Serializability: Linearizability ensures recency of single register reads/writes; Serializability ensures multi-operation transaction isolation without race conditions.
Unreliable Clocks: Physical NTP clocks drift; systems must rely on logical clocks (Lamport/Vector) or bounded uncertainty intervals (Spanner TrueTime).
Consensus Equivalence: Distributed consensus, atomic broadcast, 2PC, and fault-tolerant leader election are formally reducible to each other.

title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces (OSTEP)
author: Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau & Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau
oneLiner: First-principles deep dive into Virtualization (CPU & Memory), Concurrency (Threads & Locks), and Persistence (File Systems & RAID).
keyLearnings: Virtual Memory Translation: Hardware TLB lookups, multi-level page table traversals, page faults, and kernel Copy-On-Write (COW).
Locks & Futexes: Spinlocks burn CPU cycles under contention; Linux futex provides zero-syscall fast paths in user-space with kernel sleep queues only on contention.
Crash Consistency & Journaling: Ordered journaling vs data journaling to prevent dangling pointers and corrupt metadata across unexpected power loss.
Mechanical Sympathy: L1/L2/L3 cache line alignment, branch prediction patterns, and kernel bypass I/O (epoll, io_uring).

title: Database Internals: A Deep Dive
author: Alex Petrov
oneLiner: Engineering storage engines from slotted disk pages and ARIES recovery up to Raft, Paxos, and distributed consensus.
keyLearnings: Slotted Page Layout: Storing record offset pointers in header to support variable-length columns without fragmenting disk blocks.
ARIES Recovery: Steal/No-Force buffer management policies utilizing Redo (repeating history) and Undo (rolling back uncommitted active transactions).
Compaction Strategies: Leveled vs Size-Tiered compaction trade-offs in RocksDB for write amplification vs space amplification.
Distributed Transactions: Combining Paxos consensus groups with Two-Phase Commit (2PC) to achieve high availability across shards.

title: Effective Java (3rd Edition)
author: Joshua Bloch
oneLiner: The gold-standard canon for idiomatic, robust, maintainable, and concurrency-safe Java engineering.
keyLearnings: Immutability & Defensive Copying: Eliminate shared-mutable-state bugs by default; copy constructor parameters and return defensive copies.
Generics & PECS: Producer Extends, Consumer Super (PECS) maximizes API interoperability across generic collections.
Thread Safety & Visibility: Synchronization guarantees both mutual exclusion and inter-thread memory visibility via memory barriers.
Static Factory Methods: Decouple client code from concrete implementations, enable instance-caching, and support polymorphic return types.

title: Java Concurrency in Practice
author: Brian Goetz, Doug Lea, Tim Peierls
oneLiner: The definitive theoretical and practical authority on Java Memory Model, lock-free primitives, and thread safety guarantees.
keyLearnings: Happens-Before Relationship: Volatile writes and lock releases establish transitive happens-before edges with subsequent reads.
Hardware Compare-And-Swap (CAS): Unsafe/VarHandle atomic operations for building wait-free queues and atomic state machines.
Safe Publication: How improperly initialized objects escape across thread boundaries due to CPU instruction reordering.
Thread Pool Optimization: CPU-bound pool size = N_cpus + 1; I/O-bound pool size = N_cpus * (1 + Wait_Time / Service_Time).

title: Understanding Distributed Systems
author: Roberto Vitillo
oneLiner: A practical modern guide on fault domains, backpressure, distributed tracing, and resilience patterns.
keyLearnings: Failure Domains & Cell Architecture: Partitioning microservices into autonomous cells to isolate blast radius during catastrophic outages.
Sagas vs 2PC: Distributed business workflows should use asynchronous orchestrators and compensating transactions rather than blocking 2PC locks.
Backpressure & Queue Saturation: CoDel and adaptive concurrency limits to drop requests gracefully before servers thrash and crash.
Idempotency Keys: Leveraging unique client UUIDs in Redis/PostgreSQL with conditional inserts to prevent duplicate processing.

title: System Design Interview (Vol 1 & 2)
author: Alex Xu & Sahn Lam
oneLiner: Pragmatic, interview-tested architectural blueprints for hyperscale distributed services and real-time platforms.
keyLearnings: System Design 4-Step Framework: Requirement scoping, high-level architecture, deep-dive into bottlenecks, and operational wrap-up.
Distributed Rate Limiting: Sliding window log and token bucket algorithms implemented via atomic Redis Lua scripts.
Distributed Unique IDs: Twitter Snowflake bit-allocation architecture generating strictly monotonic IDs without single points of failure.
Distributed Message Queue: Log partition segmentation, zero-copy socket transfers, and consumer group rebalance protocols.

title: Fundamentals of Software Architecture
author: Mark Richards & Neal Ford
oneLiner: An engineering approach to architectural characteristics, trade-off analysis, modularity, and evolutionary fitness functions.
keyLearnings: The Law of Architecture Trade-offs: Every architecture decision sacrifices something (simplicity, latency, or consistency); there are no silver bullets.
Architectural Fitness Functions: Automated test suites (e.g., ArchUnit) enforcing cyclic dependency rules and layer boundaries in CI/CD.
Coupling & Instability: Calculating afferent vs efferent coupling to position services along the Normalized Distance from Main Sequence.
Modular Monoliths: Achieving domain decoupling via strict module boundaries before paying the network serialization penalty of microservices.

title: Database System Concepts (7th Edition)
author: Silberschatz, Korth, Sudarshan
oneLiner: The canonical academic text on relational query planning, cost optimization, multi-version concurrency control (MVCC), and ARIES.
keyLearnings: Query Optimization & Cost Estimation: Histogram statistics, selectivity estimation, and System-R dynamic programming join ordering.
Concurrency Control Algorithms: Strict 2PL vs Snapshot Isolation (MVCC) vs Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC).
Index Structures: B+ Tree page balancing, internal node routing, and fill-factor optimizations for SSD random reads.
Buffer Pool Management: Clock algorithm and LRU-K replacement policies under high memory pressure.

title: Monolith to Microservices
author: Sam Newman
oneLiner: Evolutionary patterns for decomposing large relational monoliths into decoupled microservices without downtime.
keyLearnings: Strangler Fig Migration: Incrementally intercepting and rerouting monolithic endpoints behind reverse proxies.
Database Decomposition Patterns: Branch-by-abstraction, dual-writing with shadow verification, and Change Data Capture (CDC).
Shared Database Anti-Pattern: Microservices must never query each other's databases directly; data boundaries must be strictly encapsulated.
Contract Testing: Consumer-driven contract testing with Pact to prevent breaking API regressions across teams.

title: C++ Concurrency in Action (2nd Edition)
author: Anthony Williams
oneLiner: Deep dive into the modern C++20 memory model, atomic operations, lock-free concurrent data structures, and thread pools.
keyLearnings: C++ Memory Order Semantics: std::memory_order_relaxed, acquire/release synchronization, and sequential consistency.
Lock-free Queue Design: Single-producer single-consumer ring buffers utilizing atomic head/tail indices with hardware memory fences.
ABA Problem Mitigation: Tagged pointers and hazard pointers for safe memory reclamation in lock-free lists.
Thread Synchronization: std::scoped_lock for multi-mutex dead-lock avoidance and condition variable spurious wakeup protection.

title: API Security in Action
author: Neil Madden
oneLiner: Zero-trust API architectures, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, cryptographic tokens, rate limiting, and defensive API gateways.
keyLearnings: Capability-based Security: Macaroons and biscuit tokens providing append-only cryptographic caveats for decentralized delegation.
Token Security: Preventing JWT signature bypasses, 'none' algorithm exploits, and implementing short-lived tokens with refresh rotation.
Mutual TLS (mTLS): Service-to-service cryptographic authentication and encrypted wire transport in zero-trust mesh networks.
Defense-in-Depth: Rate limiting, input sanitization, and request signing to thwart replay attacks.
